name: Crucible Industries Scatterpulse SP-1 'Static Cling'
description:
A compact electromagnetic scatter pistol that fires a burst of electrostatically charged micro-pellets designed to adhere to conductive surfaces on impact. Unlike conventional scatter weapons that rely on kinetic penetration, the Scatterpulse's pellets are coated with a conductive adhesive polymer that bonds to metal, carbon composite, and cyberware housings. Once adhered, the pellets discharge their stored charge in a cascading pulse that disrupts electronic systems and causes involuntary muscle contractions in biological tissue adjacent to cybernetic implants.

The SP-1 was developed as a non-lethal compliance tool for corporate security details tasked with subduing augmented individuals without destroying expensive cyberware. The pellets' adhesive coating means they cannot be simply brushed off — removal requires a solvent or careful mechanical extraction, during which the pellets continue their intermittent discharge cycle. Targets hit by the Scatterpulse describe the experience as being covered in electric bees.

Crucible markets the weapon as Tier 2 compliant on the basis of its non-lethal classification, though emergency medical reports document at least twelve cardiac events linked to Scatterpulse discharges interacting with thoracic cyberware. Crucible maintains that these incidents resulted from 'pre-existing implant conditions' rather than weapon effects.
specifications: pellet_count: ~400 per cartridge effective_range: 3-12 meters rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic, 1 shot per 0.6 seconds capacity: 8-cartridge magazine weight: 1.4 kg power_source: Integrated charge cell, 40 shots discharge_duration: 90 seconds per pellet after adhesion
tactical_use: Security teams use the Scatterpulse to disable augmented targets without engaging in physical confrontation. A single well-placed shot coats a target's cybernetic limb or torso augmentation in discharging pellets, causing involuntary spasms and system disruption that renders most aug-dependent individuals temporarily helpless. The weapon is most effective against heavily augmented targets — the more cyberware a person carries, the more conductive surfaces the pellets can bond to. Against unaugmented individuals, the weapon causes painful but manageable skin irritation.
cultural_context: The Scatterpulse has earned genuine hatred in GLMZ's augmented communities. It is viewed as a weapon designed to punish people for their cyberware — to turn their body modifications into liabilities. The phrase 'getting clinged' has entered slang as a description of any situation where a person's strengths are weaponized against them. Several aug-rights advocacy groups have filed legal challenges against the SP-1's non-lethal classification, citing the cardiac incident reports.
story_hooks: A modified Scatterpulse has appeared that fires pellets with a 48-hour discharge cycle instead of 90 seconds — targets are incapacitated for days. Someone has weaponized the compliance tool.
An aug-rights activist has developed a spray-on coating that neutralizes Scatterpulse adhesion — and Crucible Industries wants the formula suppressed.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular compact pistol with a widened muzzle assembly that tapers to a flared scatter-projection head. The profile suggests clinical precision wrapped in corporate aesthetic—all sharp edges and minimalist lines, clearly engineered for boardroom presentations before field deployment.
physical_description.dimensions: 18cm length, 11cm height, 4.5cm width at widest point. Muzzle flare extends 3cm beyond barrel terminus.
physical_description.weight_description: Light and balanced, feeling almost insubstantial in the palm—the integrated charge cell is distributed through the frame rather than concentrated in a magazine, creating an unexpectedly nimble handling profile despite its lethal potential.
physical_description.primary_material: Titanium-aluminum alloy frame with carbon-composite muzzle assembly. Internal charge cell encased in reinforced polymer.
physical_description.finish: Brushed silver-gray anodized aluminum with matte charcoal carbon-composite accents. No reflective surfaces—designed to avoid board-meeting glint.
physical_description.color_scheme: Steel gray primary with charcoal composite accents. Subtle cyan LED charge indicators recessed into the slide.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with subtle ergonomic ridges, treated with an anti-slip coating. Cool to the touch.
distinctive_features: Flared muzzle head with micro-perforation ports (barely visible pitting across the discharge face)
Recessed cyan charge-status LED strip running along the slide
Angular trigger guard with serrated upper edge
Cartridge window on the right side showing micro-pellet load status
Faint etched circumferential grooves around the muzzle (heat dissipation)
Subtle wear patterns on grip edges (field use despite 'pristine' marketing)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Crop Sciences logo—a stylized cellular helix—etched into the slide above the cartridge window. Serial plate mounted on the left frame: small raised numerals with QR-code equivalent. 'SCATTERPULSE SP-1' stamped in clean sans-serif font beneath the muzzle.
physical_description.condition_typical: Kept in meticulous condition by corporate security teams who understand the reputational cost of a malfunctioning compliance tool. Minor scuff marks on grip from regular training. Occasional micro-pellet residue visible in cartridge window. Internal charge cell shows standard degradation patterns after 100+ deployments.
